construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Depth amplifying depth — perceptual intelligence running without form
candidates.k2_overview: Your Water moves as the Twin: a current that keeps its own channel while running beside others. You match people without merging into them, fluent in company, private in depth. Two rivers to the same sea is your model of friendship: shared direction, separate water, and no argument about whose current is whose.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy runs in currents: even output for weeks, then a quiet season to refill the source.

k2_domain_readings.Peers: Your peers are parallel currents: fellow travelers heading the same direction by different beds. You collect companions across every landscape you cross. Keep a few for the whole length of the river, not just the pretty stretches.
k2_domain_readings.Independence: Water independence is having your own source: income, opinions, and inner weather that no one else controls upstream. Protect the headwaters. Everything else about you can flex.
k2_domain_readings.Self-reliance: You route around what others need rescuing from, so smoothly that nobody notices there was an obstacle. Occasionally say the obstacle out loud. Even self-sufficient rivers deserve witnesses.

angles.drive: Carrying your own weight is the first thing you do. Being a load on nobody feels like safety, so you carry what is yours rather than hand a corner to a peer. If you carry it beside someone once, it gets lighter without getting smaller.
angles.cost_self: Carrying everything yourself is what steadies you most. Water runs short in you before the week does, and you keep each load rather than share it. Set one weight down with a peer, and the rest you never take comes back to you.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you carry the whole weight yourself, you leave the people beside you nothing to hold. You put the load ahead of the closeness sharing brings. You give them a way to matter to you each time you let them carry a little.

angles.drive: An even pace is how you get through everything. You carry little Water, so you keep one steady pace rather than match every start and stop around you. If you keep it through a crowded week, you arrive with something left.
angles.cost_self: Your even pace holds you up through a long week. Little Water comes in, and you spend it steadily rather than in bursts. If you break the pace for one chance a season, you lose fewer quick chances to your own even pace.
angles.cost_others: Keeping an even pace leaves the people near you to match it or go on alone. You put your pace ahead of theirs, and a hurried friend walks a stretch alone. When you match theirs for one outing, you walk beside them rather than apart.

angles.drive: Deciding alone is your default. Asking around feels like handing over what is yours, so you decide by yourself ahead of a second view. If you ask one peer before the next big choice, you lose no speed and gain a second pair of eyes.
angles.cost_self: Alone with a decision, you are at your most sure. You keep the choice yours rather than take a second opinion, the one place blind spots get named. Letting a friend read the next big plan first keeps your mistakes smaller than it.
angles.cost_others: Each time you decide alone, you decide for the people it touches too. You settle it first, and a peer hears the plan instead of shaping it. You hand them a say in what they live with by bringing one of them in early.

angles.drive: Being hard to reach is where you rest. You hold more Water than you show, so you keep your warmth out of reach rather than let anyone feel it. Keep in mind that you want someone to reach you all the same.
angles.cost_self: Out of reach is where your depths feel safe. More Water sits in you than you move, so you would rather be useful than known. You give up closeness each time you stay out of reach, and it rarely comes back on its own.
angles.cost_others: Staying hard to reach leaves the people who love you guessing. You keep closeness in reserve rather than spend it, and they get your help in place of your company. You make the people closest to you do all the reaching.

angles.drive: Never asking is a rule you keep and never say. Water piles up in you unshared, so you manage alone rather than ask a peer for an hour. You have taught everyone around you that you need nothing, and the lesson stuck.
angles.cost_self: Managing without asking is what you do best. The Water in you runs deeper than anyone sees, and you choose doing it alone rather than asking for company. You miss out on the rest that help would have given you.
angles.cost_others: Each time you never ask, you take away a friend's chance to be useful. You keep the need to yourself rather than hand a peer one small job. You leave your peers at a distance, with nothing of yours to help with.

angles.drive: Expecting the same of everyone keeps your standard honest. You hold yourself to a hard line, and you hold your peers to it rather than to their own. You measure people by a rule they never agreed to, and few can match it for long.
angles.cost_self: Rarely let down, you hold everyone to the same standard. Water runs deep and stays hidden, and you would rather keep your own rule than lower it for company. You lose a lot of good company while waiting for the perfect match.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you expect the same from a peer, you hand them your standard without asking for theirs. You judge their effort by your own rather than by what they had to give. You hold back the credit their effort had already earned.

edge.lead: Water runs through your family, your growth and your social life. It is the same you who comes home on good days and bad, the choice you make alone and stand by either way, and the friends you choose when being alone already suited you.
